rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters imagine their deities will shield them from God’s grasp, but this baseless hope will be exposed on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: They will see the consequence of this baseless desire on the Day of Judgement.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth belong wholly to God’s dominion, and all return to Him alone; no one shares His sovereignty.
rows.anchor: Neither does anyone else have any share in His dominion nor is anyone else the being to whom people will return.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because belief in the Hereafter entails heavy accountability, people who resist its obligations deny it or invent polytheism and intercession to evade them.
rows.anchor: people who want to evade these responsibilities seek refuge in polytheism and intercession.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of God alone frightens them with the Hereafter, while mention of their alleged deities comforts them with a supposed license to follow base desires.
rows.anchor: as soon as tawh@īd is mentioned before them, their hearts start sink because at that time the Hereafter stares them in the eye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is instructed to pray for his people and entrust their matter to God.
rows.anchor: he should consign the matter of people to God;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though worldly attachment drives idolaters to devise ways around the Hereafter, when Judgment comes they will wish to ransom themselves with all earthly wealth and more.
rows.anchor: they would like that if they have whatever is in the earth and an equal more to give it in ransom for the torment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People indulge their desires and see no immediate reckoning, so they dismiss warnings of God’s justice as imagined; His gracious forbearance hides the justice they will face.
rows.anchor: he regards this to be a fabrication of one’s imagination; he thinks that if ever the Hereafter is going to come

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should ask God, Creator of the heavens and knower of the seen and unseen, to resolve people’s disputes; perfect justice will establish that God is just and wise.
rows.anchor: He shall definitely bring about a day in which His perfect justice shall manifest itself.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As already explained in 39:8, a person calls on God in hardship but, after relief, forgets God and the hardship and credits another person or his own planning and science for the blessing.
rows.anchor: once the Almighty relieves him of this hardship and blesses him with His favours, man forgets both God and the hardship

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Crediting blessings to another person or oneself is shirk: God alone grants them, while other people are only means and human abilities and science are gifts whose success depends on His permission.
rows.anchor: Both these cases are nothing but polytheism; this is because the favour a person receives is from God alone

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every favor tests whether a person gives thanks or responds with arrogance; most people miss this and fall into shirk and anarchy, as the story of Qarun illustrates.
rows.anchor: through them He actually tries and tests His servants whether they show gratitude to Him or show arrogance and haughtiness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant Quraysh repeat a claim made by earlier peoples, including Qarun, who credited wealth to his expertise; when God seized him and his treasures, neither knowledge nor strategies helped.
rows.anchor: one of them was Qārūn (Korah). It is said that whoever was afflicted with this conceited notion could not benefit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh who commit this oppression will soon face the evil results of their deeds and earnings, and they will not escape when God seizes them.
rows.anchor: they will soon face the results of their evil deeds and what they earned in an evil way

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision does not depend on human planning or authority: God gives abundantly or sparingly as He wills, as shown by unequal fortunes, hard work without gain, and sudden reversals of wealth and status.
rows.anchor: sustenance and blessings relate to man’s planning and authority; on the contrary, all of it is based on God’s wisdom and will.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distribution of provision shows God’s sole sovereignty to give or take, so people should place their trust in Him.
rows.anchor: The sovereignty of this universe lies in the hands of God. It is in His power alone to give people and in His power alone to take away from people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi contrasts this verse’s wording with the parallel in Sūrah Rūm, which says “do they not see” rather than “do they not know.”
rows.anchor: The only difference is that there the words are:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some receive wealth without effort, while others work hard and have knowledge of worldly gain yet receive only what God has allotted them.
rows.anchor: There are so many people who are born with a silver spoon in their mouths without any effort

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person’s fortune can reverse overnight, showing that wealth and authority are not secured by personal plans.
rows.anchor: today a person is a millionaire or a billionaire and possesses great power and authority

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people still credit their wealth and status to their own knowledge and planning, Islahi says something is wrong with their senses.
rows.anchor: then it must be conceded that there is something wrong with his senses.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next section warns that polytheism and intercession will not save the idolaters but hasten ruin; success requires sincere turning to God and following His revealed Book, or their later regret will be useless.
rows.anchor: The path to success hinges on focussing attention towards God with sincerity of heart and on following this best of Books
